title: observability: token-level cost/latency & KV metrics dashboards + alert tuning
author: Priya Shah
commits: add token-level cost/latency metrics and tags
expose KV cache hit/miss metrics to metrics pipeline
alerting: tune SLO-based thresholds and add runbook links
docs: observability guide and dashboard playbook
tests: add end-to-end metrics ingestion tests
description:
Context: Our per-request cost attribution and latency breakdowns have limited visibility into token-level behavior and KV cache efficiency. This makes it hard to detect regressions that only appear at long tail token counts (e.g., prefix reuse, cache thrash) and to accurately attribute cost to customer requests. Motivation: provide token-level cost and latency panels, add KV cache hit/miss metrics to understand cache effectiveness, and tune alerts to reduce false positives while catching regressions early. Changes in this PR:
- Instrumentation: add token-level metrics (token_count, token_cost_usd, token_latency_ms) and labels (model, route, customer_tier, kv_hit) in telemetry/metrics. Metrics are exposed via Prometheus-compatible exporters.
- KV metrics: export kv_cache_hit{shard,model,route} and kv_cache_miss with per-token attribution; added exporter shim and tests.
- Dashboards: two new dashboards (token_cost_latency.json, kv_cache_metrics.json) with overview + focused panels: 95th/99th token latency by model, cost per 1k tokens by route, KV hit-rate heatmaps, per-route TTL churn. Panels include template variables (region/model/route) and links to runbooks.
- Alerts: moved SLO-related thresholds to percentiles (p95/p99) in observability/alerting/alerts.yaml, added dedup windows, and tuned thresholds to reduce noise during bursts. Added runbook links and playbook steps for diagnosis (how to check KV hit rate, investigate long tail tokens, fallback policy checks).
- Docs: new observability guide (docs/observability/token-level-metrics.md) with examples for interpreting dashboards and recommended remediation steps.
- Tests: end-to-end metrics ingestion test that asserts Prometheus metrics are emitted and dashboards display expected series keys.
Checklist:
- [x] Instrumentation added and unit-tested
- [x] Dashboards reviewed with SRE and product
- [x] Alert thresholds tuned and validated in staging
- [x] Docs updated with playbook
- [x] CI green
CI: All checks (unit, lint, integration, chart) passed on first run. Follow-up: We'll monitor alert firing in staging for one week and iterate on thresholds if necessary. Related: ENG-2143 (token-level observability tracking), SRE-98 (reduce alert noise).
review_comments: Ethan Cole: Overall looks good. A couple of questions: 1) token_cost_usd - where is the conversion rate coming from? We need to ensure it's stable and not recomputed per-request.

Priya Shah (author): token_cost_usd uses the per-model unit cost config (charts/observability/values.yaml) and is applied at emit-time by the collector; added note in docs and code comment. For alerts we added a 10m suppression window and a deployment label to mute canary routes; see alerts.yaml (matchers) - happy to extend if SRE wants longer.
Maya Li: Dashboards look great; can you add a small panel showing token latency distribution for requests with KV misses only? That helps isolate cache impact.
Priya Shah (author): Added KV-only latency panel to the KV dashboard and included a short explanation in the docs.
Diego Rivera: Tests are failing intermittently in the first run (metrics_ingest_test). I saw a race in the exporter startup. Can you add a retry/backoff in the test harness?
Priya Shah (author): Added backoff/retry and asserted series exist before checking values. Re-ran CI - all green. Approved.
release_notes: Add token-level cost and latency dashboards and KV cache metrics; tune alert thresholds to reduce noise and provide runbook guidance. This improves root cause diagnosis for long-tail latency and cache regressions.
